title: Releasing a rule and considering new words

captions.physics: Discussing promises in a shared language
captions.energy: Ending an exhausted form of agreement

meaning: A shared language of promises helps you end an unworkable form while leaving each person time to consider which new word they can actually give.
text: An earlier form of a familiar promise can end while its meaning still needs fresh understanding. The Hierophant in the physical position of Vishuddha provides a shared language of commitments and recognised words of participation. Death in energy supports a constructive readiness to finish what no longer works within your speech. The Hermit in emotions responds through personal reflection. A clear admission may need silence afterwards. A new promise need not be spoken immediately simply to replace one formula with another and restore outward certainty.

For example, you discuss always ending a message exchange with a lengthy farewell. One person has grown tired of the obligation; the other sees a sign of attention in it. **New words may need time after an earlier form.** You can acknowledge that the habit is exhausted and describe the meaning you want to preserve. A pause before new consent allows an actual wish to emerge before another similar ritual is established.

The difficulty appears if conversation never continues after the old rule ends. One person considers the important thing said; the other lacks an understandable reply about participation. Stating a willingness to return makes private reflection part of a shared exchange. Silence then helps change find meaning without leaving someone to guess what can now be expected from your words.
